indication.text: CRENESSITY is indicated as adjunctive treatment to glucocorticoid replacement to control androgens in adults and pediatric patients 4 years of age and older with classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH).

target_moa.text: Crinecerfont is a selective first-in-class antagonist of the corticotropin-releasing factor type 1 (CRF1) receptor; it binds CRF1 receptors and inhibits ACTH secretion from the pituitary, thereby reducing excessive production of adrenal androgens.

citations.quote: Crinecerfont is a selective antagonist of the corticotropin-releasing factor type 1 (CRF1) receptor intended to decrease ACTH stimulation of the adrenal gland's hormone production.
Crinecerfont is a selective first-in-class CRF1 receptor antagonist that reduces the excess ACTH secretion caused by elevated CRF in response to low glucocorticoid levels in patients with CAH.
Crinecerfont, a new molecular entity, is a first-in-class selective antagonist of the pituitary corticotropin-releasing factor type 1 (CRF1) receptor.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions in adults (≥4%): fatigue (25% vs 15% placebo), headache (16% vs 15%), dizziness (8% vs 3%), arthralgia (7% vs 0%), back pain (6% vs 3%), decreased appetite (4% vs 2%), myalgia (4% vs 3%). In pediatric patients: headache (25% vs 6%), abdominal pain (13% vs 0%), fatigue (7% vs 0%), nasal congestion (7% vs 3%), epistaxis (4% vs 0%). Serious concern is acute adrenal insufficiency/adrenal crisis (adrenal crisis 1.6% with crinecerfont vs 0% placebo in adults).
